explanations.text:
●  a shape fell short                                     ([the door](shapes))
  │     An abstraction did not explain enough, and the
  │     catalog that produced it sits in one folder.
  │     This skill is the only door into that folder;
  │     everything else only reads it.
  │
  ●  you show the ideal                                ([the input](The input))
  │     You bring what the shape should have looked like:
  │     a sketch, a photo, a marked screen, a rewrite.
  │     The run starts from that picture, not from a rule.
  │
  ●  claude weighs it against the catalog    ([the comparison](The comparison))
  │     Every shape's rules and example stand against
  │     the ideal, and one decision comes out: a new
  │     shape, a changed rule, or a changed example.
  │     The smallest change that would have produced
  │     the ideal wins.
  │
  ●  you give the word                       ([the validation](The validation))
  │     Claude shows the decision and the exact new text
  │     and writes nothing yet.
  │     The folder changes on your word only, and the
  │     shape file records which project validated it.
  │
  ●  the next telling lands closer                            ([the aim](Why))
        Each validated change moves the decompiler and
        the compiler nearer the perfect abstraction.

A human skill that creates shapes for the human compiler. puts it into [compiler/shapes/](e1:the door).

It's invoked when an abstraction shape didn't sufficiently explain. And it required [input](e1:the input) on what would an ideal shape would've looked. Each shape comes with rules and a general example so it's easier to understand when to use.

The input [compares](e1:the comparison) to the current shapes on the folder, its rules and the example and takes a [decision](e1:the validation) on whether to add a new shape. add or modify rules or modify the example. So the next time the decompiler or compiler has to use a shape it manages to get closer to the [perfect abstraction](e1:the aim).
